editor.fourthdimension.recovery.hint: Brake tow, stop power, then detach (max 0.75 b/s)
editor.fourthdimension.recovery.locked: Disconnect recovery before ride dispatch, opening restraints or releasing retention.
editor.fourthdimension.recovery.action_2: Close restraints and retain every car. Sneak-use the Rotation Tool on a stopped bare bearing on matching track, then attach at the correct axle spacing.
Inspect any fault and restore matching track, gear, bodies and couplings before resuming. Keep restraints closed and carriers retained. Towing never resumes automatically.
Brake the whole recovery consist, then stop its external propulsion before disconnecting.
Stop external propulsion and wait for the complete consist to stop and align. Only the recovery coupling is removed; original train links and carrier retention remain.
Stop the PAX shuttle and retain every car with closed restraints. Hand over its loaded physical winch and carriage before attaching recovery.

After restoring the exact original matching section, keep restraints closed and carriers captured. Repair validates the stored geometry only; then use Realign matching track before dispatch. Changed geometry requires an unoccupied profile rebind.
After Repair matching track, realign the stopped native chassis with the exact repaired section. This physically re-engages the native bearing and keeps riders, restraints and carrier capture intact.

fourthdimension.ponder.matching.header: Match the car to its functional track
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_1: Each 4D family needs its own matching track. The colored strips here are route diagrams.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_2: Arrow, Legacy ZacSpin, Free Spin, Revised Free-Rotor and PAX are separate mechanisms.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_3: An appearance style changes decoration. It does not turn ordinary track into 4D track.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_4: Only verified fitting ordinary adapters can use the main rails. They receive no 4D seat effects.
fourthdimension.ponder.matching.text_5: Keep disabled 4D cars on matching track. Ordinary rail access does not certify recovery towing.
fourthdimension.ponder.construction.head: Connect anchors and assemble a matching car
fourthdimension.ponder.construction.text: Place native Coasters anchors. Use the family track item on the first anchor, then the second.
Sneak-click with the track item to cancel a selection. Continue the route with the same family.
These colored blocks illustrate a route; they are not track blocks to place. Shape the real connection with native Coasters tools.
Use the matching car item on a connected anchor. Clear the whole rotating seat and rider corridor.
Use the Rotation Tool on an anchor to edit its section. Rebind profiles after changing track geometry.
The chassis needs propulsion from Create or the native chain system. Seat rotation does not drive the train.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_1: The Arrow car has four seats on two driven wing carriers. It requires Controlled 4D Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_2: This is a motion diagram. In the ride, paired followers read the control rails; a rack and 8:1 gear train drive the real carrier axle.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_3: The car follows the profile on its bound section. Edit that section's keys as distance:degrees[:slope], separated by semicolons.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_4: Keep a full turn as 360 degrees, not zero. Place the car on the section with the profile you authored.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_5: The exposed spring allows limited tracking lag. During capture or acquisition the clutch opens, so a non-neutral rail does not pretend to drive a neutral seat.
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_6: Capture and align both carriers before boarding. Close restraints before releasing capture and dispatching; the clutch re-engages after the axle acquires its target.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_1: The Legacy ZacSpin car has eight seats on two back-to-back carriers. Use Legacy ZacSpin Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_2: Gravity, track motion and rider loading drive its free rotation. Section angle keys do not drive these carriers.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_3: The groups can respond differently. Use the Rotation Tool on the car to tune damping and ballast.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_4: This diagram illustrates free motion; it is not a prediction of a particular ride's spin.
fourthdimension.ponder.legacy.text_5: Request capture, then wait for both carriers to align and stop before opening restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.header: Four independently rotating Free Spin pairs
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_1: The Free Spin car has eight seats in four paired carriers. It requires Magnetic Free Spin Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_2: Each group has its own free hinge. Rider loading and motion can give the groups different responses.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_3: Matching track accepts magnetic spans. Inducers add torque; dampers oppose angular velocity.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_4: Select span targets with the Rotation Tool. The animation is an illustration, not an exact manufacturer coupling model.
fourthdimension.ponder.free_spin.text_5: Damping is not a boarding lock. Capture all four carriers and wait for readiness before unloading.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_1: The Revised Free-Rotor car has eight seats in four independent pairs. Use Revised Free-Rotor Track.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_2: Its lower hinges and chassis differ from the Free Spin car. They need their own matching mechanism and clearance.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_3: Tune damping and ballast on the car. Section rotation keys do not drive its free carriers.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_4: Compare the groups under different rider loading. This is an original inspired variant, not exact manufacturer coupling.
fourthdimension.ponder.revised.text_5: Stop the chassis, capture every group and wait for alignment before opening restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.header: Induce spin, damp spin, then capture
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_1: Use an Inducer or Damper on a Magnetic Free Spin section to install a span.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_2: Edit its start and end distances, direction, strength, falloff and target mask with the Rotation Tool.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_3: Orange marks an inducer. Track-mounted magnetic faces act across an air gap on the selected carriers’ reaction rings.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_4: Cyan marks a damper. It opposes existing spin across the same air gap; it does not prescribe a final seat angle or mechanically latch the carrier.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_5: Targets use car-local left-front 1, left-rear 2, right-front 4, right-rear 8. Add them; 15 selects all four.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_6: Rollback does not swap these group names. Ordinary carts receive no magnetic seat assistance.
fourthdimension.ponder.magnets.text_7: Capture and readiness provide the boarding lock. A slow carrier is not automatically safe to board.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_1: Use an empty hand on the Boarding Station to bind a nearby non-PAX car. The station does not propel it.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_2: Power at the rear requests capture. Wait for a stopped chassis, aligned carriers and the front readiness signal.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_3: Board an open seat with empty hands. Use the Rotation Tool on the car to close restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_4: The right indicator reports closed restraints. Keep capture until riders are secured.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_5: Remove rear power to request dispatch. Restraints must be closed; the propulsion system moves the car.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_6: On return, request capture and wait for readiness before opening restraints and unloading onto a platform.
fourthdimension.ponder.boarding.text_7: PAX uses the winch cycle instead. Its return capture must complete before boarding or unloading.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.header: PAX catch, powered lift, release and return
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_1: Build one connected PAX track route between two spikes. The compact route shown here is a diagram.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_2: Place four PAX cars six blocks apart. Hold a Minecraft Chain, right-click one car then its neighbor, and repeat for each adjacent pair.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_3: Place a winch within twelve blocks of the stopped train. Sneak-use it to bind, then supply Create rotation at 16 to 128 RPM. This is the remote drive unit.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_4: Wait for boarding readiness. Board, close restraints and have the platform operator use the winch to start.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_5: A separate guided carriage engages the lead receiver and lifts the train. At the crest its catch releases; the train then travels freely.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_6: The shuttle passes outbound, reverses and returns. Seat rotation remains free during the ride.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_7: The returning train is caught and retained. Wait for the winch to report boarding readiness before opening restraints.
fourthdimension.ponder.pax.text_8: If lift power is interrupted, restore power, inspect the route and use the winch normally to resume. The diagram does not show a cable to the remote drive.
tooltip.fourthdimension.wing_car.1: Four fixed seats beside ordinary Coasters track. No rotary carrier or profile.
tooltip.fourthdimension.wing_car.2: Leave 4.8 blocks to either side and 3.6 above the path. Use broad curves (radius 16+) and gradual banks.
tooltip.fourthdimension.wing_car.3: Board stopped/upright, close restraints, then Dispatch. Stop before opening and unloading.
tooltip.fourthdimension.wing_car.4: Link up to two Wing cars six blocks apart. Dye an empty stopped seat to recolor all four.
message.fourthdimension.comfort.on: Rider view: world-stable (mouse look stays free)
fourthdimension.suspended.instructions: Build matching overhead track; bind a level dock and the lift section. Close restraints before dispatch. The cabin stays locked on the lift, then swings through the curves. Return to the dock to stop, align, open and unload.
fourthdimension.suspended.lock_pending: Aligning for swing lock — travel held
fourthdimension.suspended.limit: Swing limit — damping and travel stop
fourthdimension.suspended.not_docked: Stop at the bound level dock before opening restraints
fourthdimension.ponder.arrow.text_7: If tracking exceeds the spring travel, the clutch releases and the train requests stop and capture. Inspect the profile and fault before resuming.

moving.fourthdimension.decision.shallow_: Classic Spinning supports at most 30° pitch. Select the shallow tilt preset.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.wrong_in: Install the functional insert for this exact car family and variant.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.contact_: The rail contact geometry does not match the car. Replace the insert.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.mount_mi: Use the matching above-rail, overhead or Pipeline side-contact bed.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.missing_: Restore the required control, magnetic, yaw or posture interface.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.non_nati: Use original native Coasters track material. External track does not qualify.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.invalid_: Choose a straight 16, 32 or 48 block bed.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.partial_: Bring the complete homogeneous train onto the bed with both end margins.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.mixed_tr: Separate mixed families; capture one homogeneous train.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.too_many: Use at most four cars and obey this family’s lower limit.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.oversize: Use a longer bed; reserve two blocks beyond each end of the complete train.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.empty_se: The ordinary service configuration permits empty native carts only.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.custom_n: Custom native bodies are unsupported. Use an original supported car.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.carrier_: Stop and retain every chassis and moving carrier before moving the bed.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.restrain: Close every occupied restraint before capture or movement.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.still_ro: Stop every car and carrier before capturing the train.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.invalid_: Restore the family’s required route and safe posture before capture.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.destinat: Clear and restore the exact receiving span, then reserve it again.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.obstruct: Clear the complete occupied sweep, including seats, carriers and guides.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.propulsi: Release competing propulsion ownership before moving-track capture.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.managed_: Move this train outside the managed 1.2 circuit before capture.
moving.fourthdimension.decision.launch_s: Launch Systems handoff is outside 1.5. Use native fixed approaches.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.0: Construction: place the matching controller and connect real Create power to its rear shaft. Open the front panel. Choose the exact car configuration, a 16/32/48 block bed, its world origin and cardinal direction. Preview spends nothing. Cyan outlines show the full moving structure sweep; gold outlines show fixed machinery; green boxes identify native dock anchors. Socket positions lists exact block coordinates. Close the panel to place native anchors while nearby preview ghosts remain visible; Clear preview removes them. Clear the sweep and validate. Build then consumes the server-listed parts and functional insert modules. After Build, use the normal matching track tool to connect fixed approach rails to the exact sockets; Capture refuses until they are valid. Existing curves on a shifted or angled socket must be removed and rejoined after Build. Keep the controller outside the sweep and within eight blocks when operating.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.1: Parts and survival: craft bed beams, overhead gantries or Pipeline side-contact beds, guides, pivots, end locks and docking sockets. Each has its own recipe. The matching controller uses a precision mechanism and the relevant Create drive component. Craft the exact family insert with its normal track item plus eight iron ingots: eight modules per recipe, one module per bed-length block. Skins, colors and car body variants never grant mechanical compatibility. The panel shows the exact structural bill before Build.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.2: Operating and recovery: board at a fixed station, close restraints and stop the complete train on the bed. Capture retains all chassis and carriers. Choose a destination, then Move. Release requires the real bed to stop and align, locks to engage and the exact receiving rail to be reserved and reconnected. Power loss, obstruction, broken support, unload and restart hold the train. Inspect the cause and use explicit Resume or Return; no saved release flag grants permission. Evacuation requires stationary retained bodies and safe measured exits. Never board, couple or repaint while retained.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.3: Wing transfer example: choose Wing, length 16 and translation 4. With origin (0,80,0) facing south, the starting rail anchors are (0,80,-8) and (0,80,8); the second span is four blocks east. Place matching original native approach rails. Preview and build the visible bed, outboard guides and locks. Board one Wing car at a fixed station, stop it wholly within the bed, close restraints, Capture, Move to end, then Release only after measured locking.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.4: Wing turntable example: choose Wing, length 16, ports 0° to 90°. Preview marks the two perpendicular fixed spans around the same center. Build each approach with the normal track tool; keep the full circular sweep clear. The full-show option performs an extra bounded turn before the same named exit. Never use a visual heading alone as docking evidence: the panel’s measured locks and release guards remain authoritative.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.5: Dive drop example: choose Dive, length 16 and drop 4. Install Dive inserts and matching native Dive approach rails at the upper and lower sockets. Clear the vertical sweep below all six seats. The downward stroke is bounded, not free fall; the reset is powered. Capture the complete stopped car, Move to the lower dock, Release after locking, then return the empty bed explicitly.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.6: Wing tilt example: choose Wing and 30° or 90° tilt. The bed pivots at its center. Exact angled socket positions are computed from the finite program; never round the rail endpoint geometry to a block grid. The visible native anchor identifies the socket while the native rail attaches at its exact endpoint. Keep the full pitched train and rider sweep clear. Classic Spinning may use only the 30° option.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.7: Classic Spinning elevator example: choose Classic Spinning S1, length 16 and lift 4, 8, 16 or 32. Use S1 inserts, a real elevated receiving span and full-height guides. Close restraints and latch the local spinning carrier before capture. This level lift does not grant S1 inverted/90° tilt capability. A stopped lift with lost power remains held until an explicit recovery request passes inspection.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.8: Wing teeter example: choose Wing, length 16 and one to three cycles. Build one starting dock and clear the complete ±15° pitch sweep. Capture only a stopped complete train. The finite show returns to its original level pose; Release still waits for measured locks. Do not place approach scenery, riders or machinery inside the teeter envelope.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.9: S2 side-drop example: choose S2, length 16 and side-drop 4 or 8. The bed stays level while translating diagonally down and sideways by the selected amount. Preview locates the second fixed span and the combined sweep. Retain the spinning carrier before capture. Build the second real receiving track before movement; this is not a teleport between disconnected anchors.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.10: S2 compound and alternate mount examples: compound combines the shortest yaw turn (at most 180°) with +15° or -15° pitch and finishes level at the selected port. Use the full simultaneous sweep. For suspended families choose an overhead gantry, leaving the under-rail rider space open. For Pipeline choose its distinct low side-contact bed. Compatibility lists all 22 configurations and limits; only original supported pairings can be built.
moving.fourthdimension.materials_preview: Request a preview to see the exact material list.
moving.fourthdimension.sockets_preview: Request a preview to list exact native anchor blocks.
moving.fourthdimension.sockets_teaching: Place native anchor blocks at these positions. Build the assembly before joining matching approach rails to its exact sockets. Nearby preview ghosts remain visible after closing the panel; Clear preview removes them.
moving.fourthdimension.mount.between_sid: low side-contact bed with end portals
